I just finished Cyptonomicon (Neal Stephenson) on audio book last night. At 43 hours it the longest book I've listened to so far, but I wish it was even longer. The story is almost not sci fi but rather fiction about science, namely cryptography and computer science in general. I have read the first of Stephenson's Baroque Cycle earlier, and now I want to read the rest; they tie in in many obvious and quite a few not-so-obvious ways, which rewards the observant reader.

I don't see any reason to silence discussion. If someone is selling steroids illegally and advertising as such, yeah, that should be shut down. In general, I don't think we should allow advertising.

But absolutely, I don't think information should be construed as bad. If people had horror stories of their experiences or if they had success and happiness trying it out and they wanted to share what they did and how it helped, then I think those stories from both sides should be encouraged as they allow us to see both sides of the argument and make our own conclusions.

Myself, I won't do steroids. I think one of my proudest moments when really getting started into fitness was when people started accusing me of taking them, that's how I knew I was doing things right. I'll never look like Arnold, Sylvester, Mark McGuire or any of those guys, but that's OK with me personally. I just wanted to get fit and healthy, and I've done a lot towards those goals so far, even if I have a long road to travel yet. I won't disparage people who take them UNLESS they are taking them while active in a combat sport like MMA, Thai boxing, boxing, etc., as at that point I'd consider taking them cheating. If you're taking them for personal reasons only though, I don't think you should be shamed.
